links.outcome: Workload, cancer detection, and recall when AI-classified low-risk exams skip radiologist reading
links.effect: Compared with standard double reading of all exams, the AI strategy cut workload 63.6%. Cancer detection rose 15.2% (6.3 to 7.3 per 1,000). Recall rose 14.8%, failing noninferiority.
links.quote: In the AI strategy, radiologist workload was 63.6% lower; the cancer detection rate was 15.2% higher (95% confidence interval 6.6%, 24.4%), increasing from 6.3 of 1,000 to 7.3 of 1,000, P < 0.001; and the recall rate was not noninferior and was 14.8% higher (95% confidence interval 9.0%, 20.6%).

unlisted_practices: Partially autonomous AI triage that assesses low-risk screening mammograms as normal without radiologist reading, with remaining exams double read with AI support

links.effect: Radiologist workload decreased in digital mammography (-62.1%) and digital breast tomosynthesis (-65.5%).
links.quote: Subanalyses by modality highlighted a similar workload reduction in digital mammography (-62.1%) and digital breast tomosynthesis (-65.5%).

links.outcome: Workload, cancer detection, and recall with versus without radiologist reading of every case
links.effect: Skipping low-risk reads reduced workload by 63.6%; cancer detection increased from 6.3 of 1,000 to 7.3 of 1,000; recall was 14.8% higher and did not meet noninferiority.
links.quote: In the AI strategy, radiologist workload was 63.6% lower; the cancer detection rate was 15.2% higher (95% confidence interval 6.6%, 24.4%), increasing from 6.3 of 1,000 to 7.3 of 1,000, P < 0.001; and the recall rate was not noninferior and was 14.8% higher (95% confidence interval 9.0%, 20.6%).

links.effect: Automating low-risk case review while routing other cases to humans lowered workload by 63.6% and increased cancer detection by 15.2%.
links.quote: In the AI strategy, radiologist workload was 63.6% lower; the cancer detection rate was 15.2% higher (95% confidence interval 6.6%, 24.4%), increasing from 6.3 of 1,000 to 7.3 of 1,000, P < 0.001; and the recall rate was not noninferior and was 14.8% higher (95% confidence interval 9.0%, 20.6%).

links.effect: Excluding AI-designated low-risk exams from human review lowered workload by 63.6% and increased cancer detection by 15.2%, contrary to requiring universal human review.
links.quote: In the AI strategy, radiologist workload was 63.6% lower; the cancer detection rate was 15.2% higher (95% confidence interval 6.6%, 24.4%), increasing from 6.3 of 1,000 to 7.3 of 1,000, P < 0.001; and the recall rate was not noninferior and was 14.8% higher (95% confidence interval 9.0%, 20.6%).

links.effect: The AI strategy's impact on cancer detection and recall rates differed depending on whether digital mammography or digital breast tomosynthesis was used.
links.quote: However, in digital mammography, the cancer detection rate increased by 1.6 of 1,000 and the recall rate by 1.3%, while both remained stable in digital breast tomosynthesis.

screen.practice: AI triage excluding low-risk exams from radiologist reading, with AI-supported double reading
screen.reason: This is a prospective paired noninferiority clinical trial evaluating a partially autonomous AI triage deployment strategy (autonomous rule-out of low-risk exams plus AI-supported double reading) versus standard double reading.

primary.practice: AI-based triage and autonomous rule-out of low-risk screening cases
